reasoning_traces.think:
The two neural principles form a dual mechanism for behavioral adaptation: one temporal (perseverative trace), the other combinatorial (pattern discrimination). Perseverative traces enable short-range temporal integration by maintaining sensory relevance beyond immediate stimulus presence, supporting survival-based continuity. Pattern discrimination introduces stochastic variability into repeated stimuli, allowing organisms to distinguish nuanced environmental configurations. These mechanisms jointly support a layered cognitive architecture where temporal coherence enables dynamic response alignment, while pattern variance allows for flexible categorization. The failure mode of either mechanism—either trace decay too rapidly or insufficient trace variation—results in maladaptive behavior. Temporal integration fails when trace duration cannot span relevant environmental dynamics; pattern discrimination fails when variability is too low to encode distinctions.
